title: 2023 AMC 10B Problem 11
statement: Suzanne went to the bank and withdrew \(\$800.\) The teller gave her this amount using \(\$20\) bills, \(\$50\) bills, and \(\$100\) bills, with at least one of each denomination. How many different collections of bills could Suzanne have received?

solutions.text: Let \(a, b, c \ge 1\) count the \(\$20, \$50, \$100\) bills. Then \(20a + 50b + 100c = 800,\) which divides down to \(2a + 5b + 10c = 80.\) Both \(2a\) and \(10c\) are even, so \(5b\) is too, forcing \(b = 2t.\) Now \(a = 40 - 5t - 5c \ge 1\) means \(t + c \le 7.\) With \(t, c \ge 1,\) the pairs number \(1 + 2 + \cdots + 6 = 21.\) Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Divide \(20a + 50b + 100c = 800\) by \(10;\) parity then forces the number of \(\$50\) bills to be even
Writing \(b = 2t,\) count positive integer pairs \((t, c)\) with \(t + c \le 7\)
